entries.topic: Netanyahu's maps at the UN (22 Sep 2023, 27 Sep 2024) and the Philadelphi press-conference map (2 Sep 2024)

claims.text: Netanyahu addressed the 78th UN General Assembly on 22 September 2023, showing 'a map of the Middle East in 1948' ('Here is Israel in 1948 ... a tiny country, isolated') and then, with a red marker, 'the blessing of a new Middle East'; 'Peace between Israel and Saudi Arabia will truly create a new Middle East'

Same speech: 'we must not give the Palestinians a veto over new peace treaties with Arab states'; also said peace with Saudi Arabia 'will enhance the prospects of peace with the Palestinians' and that 'a real path towards a genuine peace with our Palestinian neighbors can finally be achieved'

JPost: the 1948 map showed Israel alone in green; the 2023 map showed seven countries in green including Israel and Saudi Arabia; the map placed the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem within Israel's boundaries with no Palestinian territory marked; Laith Arafeh (PA representative to Germany) and Hadar Susskind (Americans for Peace Now: 'His map of Greater Israel is perhaps the only honest part of his speech today') criticised it

German Foreign Ministry spokesman Sebastian Fischer said a map not depicting occupied or annexed territories 'is of no help' to a negotiated two-state solution; US State Department spokesman Matthew Miller declined to discuss the map and reaffirmed support for two states; Netanyahu's office had not responded to Ynet (26 Sep 2023)

At the UN on 27 September 2024 Netanyahu held two maps labelled 'The Blessing' (a normalisation corridor through the Gulf, rail and cables linking Asia to Europe) and 'The Curse' (Iran and its allies, 'Iran's arc of terror'), saying 'the line separating the blessing and the curse could not be more clear'; many delegates left as he began

Middle East Monitor, citing Anadolu Agency, reported that the 2024 maps 'did not identify the West Bank and the Gaza Strip, but showed all the territory as part of Israel'; Jewish Insider and GZERO did not address the point (Turkish/advocacy outlets only; not confirmed in Western reporting found)

At a 2 September 2024 press conference on the Philadelphi Corridor Netanyahu used a Gaza map and a map on which the West Bank appeared as part of Israel; critics included ICG's Mairav Zonszein, UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, Palestinian ambassador Husam Zomlot and Peace Now; no Israeli government clarification was reported

entries.topic: Netanyahu's i24NEWS 'Greater Israel' exchange (aired 12 Aug 2025) and the responses

claims.text: Netanyahu was interviewed by Sharon Gal on i24NEWS; the interview aired on Tuesday 12 August 2025 (date inferred from reports dated 13-14 Aug saying 'on Tuesday')

Reported wording differs: asked whether he felt connected to the vision of Greater Israel he said 'Very much' (Media Line, LBCI, New Arab); 'Very much so' (L'Orient Today); 'very attached' (New Arab 14 Aug); AFP and Al Jazeera report that asked whether he subscribed to the vision he said 'absolutely'; AFP adds 'If you ask me what I think, we're there' and a turn to Israel's 'great mission'; New Arab: 'historic and spiritual mission' and a 'mission on behalf of the Jewish people'. Hebrew original not found

Gal gave Netanyahu a piece of jewellery for Sara Netanyahu described as a 'map of the Promised Land'; it was not visible on air; Haaretz reported Gal's company sells 'Greater Israel' pendants whose outline includes parts of Egypt, all of Jordan, Lebanon, parts of Syria and parts of Iraq
Same interview, on Gaza: 'We are not pushing them out, but we are allowing them to leave'

Israeli response: per Haaretz (via L'Orient Today), the Prime Minister's Office and Foreign Ministry stressed that Netanyahu did not use the words 'Greater Israel' and is not responsible for later headlines; Jordan and Egypt sought clarifications; no on-record public clarification by the PMO was found
Jordan's Foreign Ministry: 'a dangerous and provocative escalation, a threat to the sovereignty of states'; spokesman rejected 'delusional claims'

Egypt's Foreign Ministry requested clarification, said the remarks reflected 'a rejection of peace' and that there is no way to peace 'except through a return to negotiations', reaffirming a Palestinian state on the 4 June 1967 lines

Saudi Foreign Ministry: 'complete rejection of the settlement and expansionist ideas and projects adopted by the Israeli occupation authorities'; Arab League: 'a blatant violation of the sovereignty of Arab states' / 'a serious threat to collective Arab national security'; Qatar: 'an extension of the (Israeli) occupation's approach based on arrogance'; Iraq condemned 'expansionist ambitions'; PA: 'a disregard of the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people'

Joint statement dated 16 Aug 2025 (Oman MFA) by foreign ministers of 31 states (Oman, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, Algeria, Morocco, Palestine, Iraq, Jordan, Egypt, Syria, Lebanon, Libya, Yemen, Mauritania, Sudan, Somalia, Türkiye, Bangladesh, Chad, Comoros, Djibouti, Gambia, Indonesia, Maldives, Nigeria, Pakistan, Senegal, Sierra Leone) and the secretaries-general of the Arab League, OIC and GCC: 'strongly condemn' the remarks on 'the so-called Greater Israel', 'a blatant violation of international law and a direct threat to Arab national security'; Al Jazeera says released Friday (15 Aug)
Smotrich announced plans to advance more than 3,000 housing units in E1 in the same days, saying it 'buries the idea of a Palestinian state'
